The motion related to [Australian Renewable Energy Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Renewable_Energy_Agency) and was part of Senator Hinch's attempt "[to save ARENA in its entirety](http://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2016-09-15.206.2)". ### Motion text > *(1) Page 2, clause 2 (table item 6), omit "Schedules 5 and 6", substitute "Schedule 6".*

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](http://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2016-09-15.353.1) to leave schedule 24 and table item 26 in clause 2 as they are. In parliamentary language, the majority voted for those parts to "stand as printed". The motion was put after Senator Jacqui Lambie moved a [motion](http://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2016-09-15.291.1) to oppose them. The parts related to military rehabilitation and compensation. When proposing to oppose them, Senator Lambie explained: > *What the government is proposing under the single appeal pathways, even though it has been amended by Labor, still means that this bill denies veterans a right to legal representation when forced to go against a government body stacked with government lawyers. Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 - Third Reading - Pass the bill
The Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 and explanatory memorandum were presented.
The revised explanatory memorandum for the Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 was tabled, with savings figures updated from the original Treasury-prepared version.

The cooperative process between government and opposition led to a bill achieving larger savings than initially proposed, while protecting vulnerable people on Newstart, pensions, and disability payments, opposing $100,000 university degrees and cuts to higher education, and preserving the Child Dental Benefits Schedule and carbon pollution reduction efforts.

Labor opposed cuts to the clean energy supplement for pensioners, people with disability, carers, and job seekers, and cuts to income support for those in psychiatric confinement; after negotiations these measures were amended or removed from the bill. The party will oppose any future attempts to cut the supplement, citing that a single mother on Newstart would lose $220 a year and a pensioner couple $550 a year.

The Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 secures an additional $800 million over five years for the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, preserving its research and demonstration programs, and the opposition has agreed to bipartisan discussions on accelerating clean energy transition.

The speaker argued that the Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 should be supported, but praised Labor for protecting the Child Dental Benefits Schedule—which has helped one million children—and the National Partnership Agreement on Adult Public Dental Services—which treated 400,000 adults—from being replaced by a scheme that would add five million children to public dental waiting lists.

The speaker argued that the Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 is superior to the original because it delivers larger savings, is fairer to vulnerable people, and invests in renewable energy. They also criticised the government's $50 billion tax giveaway to multinational corporations and called for further fair savings measures to protect the AAA credit rating.

The speaker supported the amended Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016, arguing that the government’s tripled deficit and 20% cut in infrastructure investment were mismanaged, and that the earlier proposal to abolish the energy supplement would have unfairly cut $4–$8 per week from the lowest-income recipients. The negotiated outcome preserved support for pensioners and vulnerable groups and secured $800 million over five years for the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA).

The Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 is a bad bill that attacks low-income earners, children's dental, and clean energy, with Labor agreeing to cut $517 million from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA)—nearly all in the next three years—while fairer alternatives like ending fuel tax credits for wealthy mining companies or reducing superannuation tax breaks for high earners were ignored.

The speaker opposed the Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016, arguing it cuts over half a billion dollars from ARENA, reduces family tax benefits and supplements, and fails to secure dental care for low-income children, while proposing alternative revenue measures such as a superprofits tax on banks and higher taxes on high earners, and criticising spending on asylum seeker detention and defence build-up.

The speaker supported the Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 while criticising the $500 million cut to the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) and calling for changes to its funding model, including repayable grants and equity stakes. They also argued for an 18-month delay to the repeal of student start-up scholarships and defended continued carbon tax compensation for low-income recipients, citing concerns for disadvantaged communities and economic demand.

The Turnbull government argued the Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill 2016 would deliver $6.3 billion in savings and reduce debt by $30 billion over the medium term, thanking the shadow Treasurer and Senator Cormann for the bipartisan agreement.

The House passed the Fair Work Amendment (Respect for Emergency Services Volunteers) Bill, which removes clauses from Victoria’s CFA enterprise agreement that gave unions power over volunteer firefighters. The speaker also noted the passage of the Budget Savings (Omnibus) Bill, saving $6.3 billion, and reported 3.3% economic growth with over 200,000 jobs created in the past year.
